title: Accelerating Rotarod: Motor Coordination and Balance Assessment in Mice
author: Sarah van Veen

steps.title: Set Rotarod to training speed
steps.instruction: Adjust the Rotarod apparatus to a constant speed of 5 rpm for the training phase.

steps.title: Train mice on Rotarod
steps.instruction: Place each mouse on the rotating rod, allow it to walk for 2 min, and if it drops, replace it (up to three times). After training, return the mouse to its home cage.

substeps.instruction: Place mouse on rod set at 5 rpm.
Allow mouse to walk for 2 minutes.
If mouse drops, place it back on the rod (repeat up to 3 times).
Return mouse to home cage after training.

steps.title: Run first accelerating trial
steps.instruction: Position the mouse on the rod at 5 rpm, start the acceleration to 40 rpm over 5 min (300 s), record latency to drop, and apply clinging rule if needed.

substeps.instruction: Place mouse on rod (ensure all four paws grip the mid‑rod) while rod is at 5 rpm.
Start acceleration protocol: increase speed from 5 rpm to 40 rpm over 5 minutes (300 seconds).
Record the time (seconds) when the mouse falls; maximum trial duration is 300 seconds.
If the mouse clings and does not walk, observe up to 3 full rotations; if still clinging, remove mouse and record the time as latency.

steps.title: Allow 10‑min rest
steps.instruction: Return the mouse to its home cage for a 10‑minute inter‑trial interval.

steps.title: Conduct remaining trials
steps.instruction: Repeat the accelerating trial and 10‑minute rest for trials 2, 3, and 4, recording latency each time.

substeps.instruction: Repeat steps “Run first accelerating trial” and “Allow 10‑min rest” for trial 2.
Repeat steps “Run first accelerating trial” and “Allow 10‑min rest” for trial 3.
Repeat steps “Run first accelerating trial” and “Allow 10‑min rest” for trial 4.

steps.title: Calculate mean latency and statistics
steps.instruction: Compute the mean latency to fall across the four trials for each mouse, express as mean ± SEM, and compare groups (e.g., WT vs KO) using appropriate statistical tests.
